title: A member pop-up that fails to send is never tried again
what: The pop-up sender moves past each batch of phones before it sends to them, so it never sends twice. But when Google's pop-up service is busy, down for a minute, or refuses our sign-in mid-batch, those members simply never get that gym message, offer or trainer reply. The failure is only counted in a log line.
expected: A pop-up that failed for a passing reason is tried again a little later, and only a pop-up that was really delivered or whose phone is gone is marked done.
how_often: every short outage of Google's pop-up service
fix_line: Keep failed phones on a short retry list and try them again in the next few runs

title: An online plan payment missed for two days is never applied and nobody is told
what: When a gym owner pays for a plan online, the payment company's call should move the plan on; a nightly check is the safety net. That nightly check only looks at payment links made in the last 48 hours, and the same link is handed out again when the owner tries later. So if the company's call fails (wrong secret, our server down) and the link is older than two days, the payment is never applied, the gym can still be cut down, and no alarm goes out. The nightly check's own failures are only a count in a log line.
expected: Every paid link that did not become a plan is found, whatever its age, and the owner is alerted the same day.
who: gym owners paying online, once online buying is switched on
how_often: rare: only when the payment company's call fails
fix_line: Check every open link until it expires, and raise an alarm when a paid link is still not applied

items.reason: server jobs only; no watch, heart rate, rest timer or workout clock code, and no device screen states here
